business_problem: A fragmented, self-managed observability stack forced engineers to jump between tools, left monitoring on the same infrastructure it monitored, and drove high AWS cost and incident blind spots.
solution_summary: DataHub replaced four self-managed observability systems with Observe by Snowflake so logs, metrics, traces, and alert context could be searched from one resilient platform. The team deployed the Observe agent across 22 EKS and GKE clusters and more than 70 isolated customer namespaces, then created separate U.S. and EU tenants through Terraform for regional data handling. Telemetry that previously lived in OpenSearch, Prometheus, Thanos, Grafana, and Alertmanager now lands in a single place where engineers can investigate incidents without switching tools or waiting for another team to build dashboards. DataHub also connected Observe’s CLI and OPAL query language to an internal AI agent in Slack, combining live telemetry with context from incident.io, Argo CD, and internal reference material. That design turns one telemetry store into both a human observability console and an AI-ready context layer for daily reports, faster diagnosis, and future automated remediation.
